figure.name: Friedrich Engels
figure.role: Writer on industrial labor, class society, and the development of socialist theory.
figure.hook: Engels = factories, class conditions, and socialism grounded in industrial life.
whyHere: Engels belongs here because he keeps the socialism road attached to industrial reality: factories, cities, wage labor, poverty, and the working-class conditions created by modern capitalism.
He is also not just Marx's shadow. Engels helped write the Manifesto, developed socialist theory in his own works, and made the industrial labor question harder to ignore.
figure.cleanIdea: If socialism is going to tell the truth, it has to look at how people actually live and work inside industrial capitalism, not only at abstract ideals.

ideas.title: Working Class
ideas.plainDefinition: The working class means people who live mainly by selling their labor rather than by owning productive property.
ideas.context: In the Engels path, working-class life is not a background detail. It is the evidence that makes the labor question concrete.
ideas.whyMatters: Working class matters for Engels because his socialism begins from real industrial conditions: wages, housing, work discipline, poverty, injury, and class power.

ideas.title: Industrial Capitalism
ideas.plainDefinition: Industrial capitalism is an economic system built around private capital, factories, wage labor, machinery, competition, and mass production.
ideas.context: In the Engels path, industrial capitalism is the historical pressure cooker that turns poverty, production, ownership, and class power into one problem.
ideas.whyMatters: Industrial capitalism matters because Engels is watching socialism emerge from a factory world, not from a clean classroom definition.

ideas.title: Scientific Socialism
ideas.plainDefinition: Scientific socialism is Engels's and Marx's claim that socialism should be explained through historical and economic forces, not only moral wishes or ideal plans.
ideas.context: In the Engels path, this term marks a break from utopian schemes toward arguments about capitalism's structure and development.
ideas.whyMatters: Scientific socialism matters because it shows why Engels is not only describing suffering. He is trying to explain where that suffering comes from and why the system changes.
